newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BRUSSELS APPROVES BAIL-OUT AT CREDIT LYONNAIS

The European Union has approved a 490 million stg bail-out of French state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, but the approval was accompanied by stern criticism of the French government for not keeping the Commission more fully aware of the problems at the bank. The bail-out will be the first step towards a new restructuring plan for the bank.
-- BT POISED FOR FRENCH TELECOMS SECTOR LINK-UP

British Telecom is expected to announce on Thursday a strategic alliance with French utilities and communications group Generale des Eaux. The deal, offering BT access to the French telecoms market, completes the British company's European coverage as it aims to become Europe's leading telecom operator.
-- SFO CHIEF DENOUNCES HANDLING OF COMPLEX FRAUD CASES

The director of the Serious Fraud Office, George Staples, has claimed that the criminal justice system has been 'emasculated' by recent judicial decisions in complex fraud trials. The comments follow the collapse last week of the case against Kevin Maxwell on pension fund fraud charges. Staples is angry with the precedent set that once one set of charges against a defendant have been dismissed, a second trial cannot take place.
-- BA MAY FACE CURBS OVER LINK-UP

The proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines is likely to be subject to a number of conditions, possibly including the surrender of some of the airlines' landing and take-off slots at Heathrow airport. The Office of Fair Trading, which is expected to report to Trade Secretary Ian Lang within days, is believed to be considering recommending that conditions be attached to the alliance.
-- ENGINEERING UNIONS PLAY 'KEY ROLE'

A report on pay in the engineering industry, compiled by independent wage research body Incomes Data Services, has found that trade unions are playing a vital role in many companies negotiating collective agreements which provide job security for workers and above-inflation pay rises in return for fundamental changes in working practices.
-- INVESTMENT IN INDUSTRY SHOWS DROP

The Office of National Statistics has reported that manufacturing investment fell by a seasonally-adjusted 5 percent between the first and second quarters of 1996, and was 7 percent lower in the second quarter than at the same time last year. However, separate figures reported a sharp decline in manufacturers' stocks in the second quarter, which may indicate that manufacturing output is set to revive strongly.
-- POWERGEN TO CEASE USE OF OIL SUBSTITUTE

PowerGen, the UK's second-largest electricity generator, has confirmed that it will cease using the controversial fuel orimulsion from next April. Orimulsion, an oil substitute, has been dubbed 'the dirty fuel' be environmentalists, who see it as the most polluting and dangerous of fuels in use. PowerGen is to make up the capacity lost through the decision by bringing back into use a coal-fired unit at Warrington.
-- YORKSHIRE CONSIDERS BUY-BACK

Regional electricity company Yorkshire Electric is considering a 120 million stg share buy-back of special dividend. The company is planning an increase in gearing, from about 45 percent to 100 percent, which will release about 120 million stg in cash. However, the move may draw criticism from the Labour party, which is planning a 'windfall tax' on the privatised utilities.
-- BT AND NEWS INTERNATIONAL PLAN INTERNET LINK

British Telecom and the media group News International have formed a joint venture company to offer an Internet service based on material from News International's leading titles, which include The Times, The Sunday Times, and the News of the World. The new company, Springboard, is intended to be home-based, and may also work with third parties to offer local news, weather, events and listings services.
-- BARRATT SAYS RIVALS OVERPAID FOR TARGETS

The chairman of housebuilder Barratt, Sir Lawrie Barratt, has attacked rivals in the industry for overpaying for acquisitions. One of the rivals is Persimmon, which pipped Barratt in the bidding to acquire Ideal Homes. Persimmon paid 169 million stg, but Sir Lawrie says Barratt valued Ideal at about 150 million stg.
